content.title: Thank you for your constructive advice:
content.comment:
1. We ignore the topology of the skeleton in this work, based on our analysis that it ignores the relationship between unconnected joints and it is not used by GCNs with a learnable topology either. The learned weights are therefore not aware of the skeleton topology but encode knowledge of the underlying joint relations. 

2. We have included the results of [2] in our revision for comparison. The model from [2] provides indeed very high scores. Yet, please note that this model is built upon CTRGCN but has significantly more parameters than others (e.g. 6.5M  versus 1.6M of InfoGCN and 2.0M for ours) and relies on a two-stage training strategy. Therefore, a direct comparison should be treated with caution.  In addition, the performance of our model might probably be improved with the help of attention mechanism, but the main purpose of our work is to reveal that many topology-centered claims do not hold and that the task of skeleton-based action recognition is not necessarily restricted to GCN frameworks.

3. We aim to solve the problem of skeleton-based action recognition, where GCN-based approaches dominate. Therefore, we revisit GCN models for this task and draw our conclusion. The revision of GCN for this task is especially significant, because the misleading observations have led follow-up works to be restricted under the GCN framework for a long time.

4. Since a GCN with learnable topology is equivalent to our FC baseline and the initialization is proved to be unimportant, they have similar performance. To compete with SOTA GCNs which also rely on **attention mechanisms**, we further propose the simple design of parallel paths and show its effectiveness experimentally in Table 2.

5. We are glad to include [1] in our revision. Unfortunately, there’s no way to download your mentioned dataset on its [homepage](https://github.com/HRI-UESTC/CFM-HRI-RGB-D-action-database). This problem is also asked in the [issues](https://github.com/HRI-UESTC/CFM-HRI-RGB-D-action-database/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue). Moreover, much fewer previous methods for skeleton-based action recognition have evaluated on this dataset, see [leaderboard](https://paperswithcode.com/dataset/uestc-rgb-d). However, we are of course happy to conduct further experiments on such data as soon as it is available for download.

We hope that we could address all your remaining concerns and are happy to discuss further questions!

content.title: Thank you for your detailed and knowledgeable review:
content.comment:
1. We actually derive our model based on the analysis that the GCNs with a learnable topology that define the current SotA in skeleton-based action recognition are equivalent to fully-connected networks. The resulting model resembles the architecture of MLP-mixer, but each layer of our model is a single linear layer instead of an MLP and the non-linearity is brought via ReLU after two consecutive spatial and channel linear layers. Unlike our model, MLP-mixer suffers from overfitting in this task and achieves poor performance in our preliminary study. Our main contribution is to show that many so-called topology-aware designs such as topology-shared GC are not really topology aware, although they appear to be. This impression (that commonly best performing GCNs are topology aware) has misled follow-up works to be restricted under the GCN framework, and our paper removes this unnecessary limitation. Therefore, we believe that our work is of significant importance to the community. 
To compete with SOTA GCNs which **also rely on attention** mechanisms, we further propose the design of parallel paths and show its effectiveness experimentally in Table 2.  

2. The different groups never communicate with each other and are only merged at the final linear layer for classification. We will describe this more clearly in the revision.

3.  Our FC baseline is equivalent to a GCN with a learnable topology except that the “adjacency matrices” are randomly initialized instead of initialized according to the topology. The initialization is proved to be unimportant in Table 1, showing that the skeleton topology does not matter for these models.

We hope that we could address all your remaining concerns and are happy to discuss further questions!

content.title: Thank you for your knowledgeable review and constructive suggestion:
content.comment:
1 a). We would like to emphasize that we don’t regard the graph convolution as a special case of fully-connected layer, but reveal that the proposed GCNs in this field are indeed fully-connected networks, i.e., GCN with learnable topology is equivalent to our FC baseline except that the initialization is different. However, we have experimentally shown in Table 1 that such a difference of initialization is negligible. This means that many so-called topology-aware designs such as topology-shared GC are not really particularly topology aware, although they appear to be. We believe that this impression (that commonly best performing GCNs are topology aware) has misled follow-up works to be restricted under the GCN framework, and our paper removes this unnecessary limitation. Therefore, we believe that our work is of significant importance to the community. To compete with SOTA GCNs which **additionally rely on attention** mechanisms, we further propose the design of parallel paths and show its effectiveness experimentally. 

1 b). For human skeleton, the number of joints should be consistent. Therefore, taking input of arbitrary size isn't the key requirement for this task.

1 c). Our model performs worse on Northwestern-UCLA but significantly better on NTURGB+D and NTURGB+D 120 than [a], probably because [a] is of a small size which fits the smallest dataset but is lack of capacity for the larger ones. 
Moreover, [a] has used their proposed data augmentation technique called SkeletonMix and data augmentation could make a hug difference for such a small dataset. 
We have included [a] in our comparison to SotA methods in our revised manuscript.

2. Since a GCN with learnable topology is equivalent to our FC baseline, such GCNs have exactly the same computation cost. In addition, our proposed design of parallel paths can be implemented as grouped 1x1 convolution which **reduces the computation** further from $O(kd^2)$ to $O(kd^2/g)$, where k, d and g refer to kernel size, channel dimension and number of groups. In contrast, SotA GCNs employ an additional attention mechanism which brings extra heavy computation.

3. We have added the effect of number of layers to our ablation study on ntu120 csub joint modality: 8 layers-84.7, 10 layers-85.4, 12 layers-85.7 (our setup), 14 layers-85.7.  

We hope that we could address all your remaining concerns and are happy to discuss further questions!

content.title: Thank you for your insightful review:
content.comment:
1. The key contribution of our paper is the revelation that recently proposed GCNs in this field are essentially fully-connected, since they	adopt a learnable adjacency matrix and its initialization is shown to be unimportant in Table 1. That is also the reason why our FC baseline performs as well as GCNs. This means that many so-called topology-aware designs such as topology-shared GC are not really topology aware, although they appear to be. We believe that this impression (that commonly best performing GCNs are topology aware) has misled follow-up works to be restricted under the GCN framework, and our paper removes this unnecessary limitation. Therefore, we believe that our work is of significant importance to the community.

2. To compete with SOTA GCNs which **additionally rely on attention** mechanisms, we further propose the design of parallel paths and show its effectiveness experimentally in Table 2. 

We hope that we could address all your remaining concerns and are happy to discuss further questions!

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper propose a fully connected layer based network for skeleton-based action recognition, which also contains a design of parallel paths for multi-relational modeling. The network achieves SOTA performance on three datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
The paper is clearly and well written. The method achieves SOTA performance.

Weakness:
The main idea of the paper is to replace GCN with fully connected layer by making the matrix A in Eq. 1 adaptive, however, this idea is not novel has been proposed in previous work.  In the paper of CTRGCN, Chen et al named this kind of network Dynamic topology-shared GC. So it is inappropriate to claim this is the innovation of this paper.
As for the experiments, it is not clear which essential factor makes the major contribution to the performance enhancement, by making A adaptive, or the design of parallel paths for multi-relational modeling or others?

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a topology-agnostic model purely based on fully-connected layers for skeleton-based action recognition. The authors revisit the concept of topology in GCN-based methods and propose to use fully-connected layers for topology-agnostic modeling. Experiments are conducted on three datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. The paper is clear and easy to understand.
2. Results on three datasets are presented on action recognition.

Weaknesses:
1. The overall ideas in the paper are not very novel. This work regards the graph convolution as a special case of fully-connected layer and proposes a model purely based on fully-connected layers. Similarly, the previous work [a] regards the graph convolution as a special case of convolution and proposes a pure CNN-based framework. More importantly, convolution is more flexible than fully-connected layer because it can take input of arbitrary size. And [a] achieves better performances than the proposed ToANet on the Northwestern-UCLA dataset (97.2% vs 96.6%). I would like the authors to provide reasonable explanation about this problem.
[a] Xu, Kailin, Fanfan Ye, Qiaoyong Zhong, and Di Xie. "Topology-aware Convolutional Neural Network for Efficient Skeleton-based Action Recognition." In AAAI, 2022.

2. For fair comparison with the state-of-the-art methods, not only the accuracy but also the computational cost should be compared in the paper.
3. The number of layers is important for ToANet. The authors should give an evaluation in the ablation study.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a topology-agnostic model based on the fully connected layers and achieves compatible performances on three skeleton action recognition datasets, compared with state-of-the-art GCN-based models.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:

(1) The proposed method achieves compatible performances based on the MLP-based model, instead of the GCN model.

Cons:

(1) From the reviewer's view, this paper is an application of MLP-Mixer on skeleton action recognition. The novelty for application is not enough; at least some specific design for the human skeleton is needed, in my opinion. 

(2) For the multi-relational modeling, if each ToA-Block is divided into the same number of paths/groups, there is only one type of relation here. 

(3) It is not clear what is Fully-Connected Baseline. Does this mean that there is no Transpose?

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents a Topology-Agnostic Network (ToANet),  which merely adopts Fully-Connected (FC) layers for skeleton-based action recognition. It is constructed by chaining FC layers applied across joints (aggregate joint information) and within each joint (transform joint features) in an alternate manner. It contains a novel design of parallel paths for multi-relational modeling.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
The ToANet merely adopts Fully-Connected (FC) layers for skeleton-based action recognition, and contains a novel design of parallel paths for multi-relational modeling. It performs better than its baseline of Yan 2018 and Cheng 2020.

Weakness:
Results comparison is limited, since it does not included some recent new publications.  
Since the revision is applied on GCN, not focusing on human actions, evaluations should be extended to other tasks, need not limits in action recognition.
Ablation study is not sufficient. The reason why the simple FC calculation outperforms relation convolution and attention mechanism should be deeply discussed.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Clarity is good, Quality need to improved, Novelty is limited And Reproducibility may be good.
content.summary_of_the_review:
1. Fig.3 is the overview of ToANet, however, it is not clear how to learn topology relationships of skeletons for the action feature learning, and the advantage of the ToANet is also not sufficiently exhibited.
2. Experiment results seem lower than published frameworks, which may need a further improvement.
3. This paper applies a pure fully-connected calculation in the GCN for feature learning. The revision is evaluated for skeleton based action recognition, but GCN is not only for this task, so if trying to certify the contribution of revisions in the ToANet, evaluations in other tasks are also required.
4. The simple fully-connected model outperforms attention based GCN, why? The attention mechanism seems more possible to obtain better and reliable performance than the simple fully-connecting. It is required to analyze the reason deeply, not simply exhibit the results. 
5. Another multi-view action dataset, the UESTC Action dataset, is a large-scale challenging action dataset, which is popularly used in previous papers. The newly proposed approach may evaluate its performance in the dataset, and compare with newly published papers.  

[1] Synthetic Humans for Action Recognition from Unseen Viewpoints, IJCV, 2021.
[2]Global-Local Cross-View Fisher Discrimination for View-invariant Action Recognition, ACMMM, 2022

content.title: Do We Really Need Graph Models for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition? A Topology-Agnostic Approach with Fully-Connected Networks
content.abstract: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have been dominating skeleton-based action recognition in recent years. While GCN-based approaches keep establishing new state-of-the-art results, the proposed architectures are getting increasingly sophisticated with a variety of add-ons. Many recent works attempt to relax the topology restriction imposed by the GCN framework, such as local/sparse connections and permutation invariance. However, the room for further innovation is extremely limited under such a framework. In this work, we present Topology-Agnostic Network (ToANet), a simple architecture based merely on Fully-Connected (FC) layers, as opposed to GCNs for skeleton-based action recognition. It is constructed by chaining FC layers applied across joints (aggregate joint information) and within each joint (transform joint features) in an alternate manner. Moreover, it contains a novel design of parallel paths for multi-relational modeling. ToANet proves to be a powerful architecture for learning the joint co-occurrence of human skeleton data. ToANet achieves better or comparable results to state-of-the-art GCNs on NTU RGB+D, NTU RGB+D 120 and Northwestern-UCLA datasets. These results challenge the convention of choosing GCNs as the de-facto option for skeleton-based action recognition. We hope that our work stimulates further research on non-GCN based methods, eliminating the restriction of topology.
